metadata.note: Wichita Falls and Southern, a single North Texas main line Wichita Falls - Archer City - Olney - Newcastle - Graham - Breckenridge - Ranger - Dublin (164.8 mi, ICC vol. 44), built in three pieces by three companies: the Wichita Falls and Southern Railway (Wichita Falls - Newcastle, 1909), the Wichita Falls & Southern Railroad (Newcastle - Jimkurn, 1921) and the Wichita Falls, Ranger & Fort Worth (Jimkurn - Breckenridge - Dublin, 1920-21). The Railway and the Railroad are one Kell-Kemp company for Rule 4; the WFR&FW ran its own trains until the WF&S Railroad took it over on 1 Sep 1927, so Breckenridge - Dublin is split at that date (shared geometry, two colours). Drawn: Wichita Falls - Newcastle 1909 [ANCHOR]; Wichita Falls - Breckenridge 1929 [OPEN] - 1942 [OPEN]; Breckenridge - Dublin 1920 - 1926 [OPEN] as the WFR&FW and 1929 [ANCHOR] as the WF&S. Passenger years are thin, and every drawn end is the last or first CONFIRMED year rather than a known start or end. The whole road was abandoned in 1954.
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 142276-142395 (Official Guide, Feb 1952 issue, WF&S tables dated 'April, 1951'; times did not survive OCR)
metadata.ownership_split: Breckenridge - Dublin: WFR&FW own operation (incl. its 1921-26 receivership) 7 Apr 1920 - 31 Aug 1927 -> feature wfrfw-breckenridge-dublin; WF&S Railroad from 1 Sep 1927 -> feature wfs-breckenridge-dublin. Wichita Falls - Newcastle: the Katy of Texas (incl. USRA) operated it 1 May 1914 - 29 Feb 1920, a real Rule 4 split, but no passenger year in that window is confirmed, so no Katy feature is drawn. The 1911 Katy stock purchase, the 1921 Railway -> Railroad lease and the 31 Dec 1940 merger are not splits.
not_yet_sourced: U1 - Wichita Falls - Breckenridge END is [OPEN]: drawn to 1942, the last confirmed year (1942 mixed Nos. 41/42 on chicagorailfan, a secondary source with no timetable cited). chicagorailfan also says passenger service was discontinued in 1950 (no source); the Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints WF&S 'Breckenridge to Wichita Falls' and 'Dublin to Breckenridge (Mon/Wed/Fri)' tables dated April 1951, but their times did not survive OCR; TSHA's 1952 revenue has no passenger line. A page image of any 1945-1951 Official Guide WF&S table or a Wichita Falls / Breckenridge 'last passenger train' newspaper story (Portal to Texas History) would settle it.

Wichita Falls - Breckenridge START is [OPEN]: 1929 rests on TSHA's system-level passenger revenue. A stricter reading would draw this feature 1942 only [ANCHOR], the one segment-specific year. Passenger trains from the July 1921 opening are implied by TSHA's 'through route' but not stated; 1921-1928 is unconfirmed.

U2 - Breckenridge - Dublin after 1929: no segment-specific passenger evidence; drawn as a 1929 [ANCHOR] on system-level revenue. The 1951 'Dublin to Breckenridge' table has no legible times. Ranger - Dublin may have lost trains well before the north end.
Breckenridge - Dublin under the WFR&FW ends 1926 [OPEN]: Jan - Aug 1927 (its operation ran to 31 Aug 1927) is unconfirmed.
Wichita Falls - Newcastle 1909 is an [ANCHOR] (Fowler's 1909G station names). 1910-1914 under the WF&S Railway and 1 Mar 1920 - 30 Jun 1921 under it again are unconfirmed and not drawn.
U3 - Katy era 1 May 1914 - 29 Feb 1920 on Wichita Falls - Newcastle: no passenger year found. A 1915-1919 Official Guide or Katy public timetable would make it drawable in Katy colour.
U4 - who ran passenger trains on Jimkurn - Breckenridge, and whether WF&S trains ran through to Dublin, Jul 1921 - Aug 1927 (separately operated companies; TSHA calls it a through route).
U5 - Wichita Falls - Newcastle opening: TSHA Sept 1908 vs ICC 1 Jan 1909; 1909 (the later date) is drawn.
U6 - Breckenridge Texan's own 1920 dates conflict (through service 'by June 27' vs first train into Breckenridge 'June 30'); the year is unaffected.
U7 - Waurika trackage rights (1927): whether WF&S passenger trains used them, and why Fowler's mileposts put Wichita Falls 35.9 mi from the timetable's zero when Waurika - Wichita Falls is 30.0.
Mileage conflict, Wichita Falls - Newcastle: 52.426 mi (ICC vol. 34) vs 55.1 (Fowler) vs 56 (a 1917 Wichita Daily Times item, reported).

Geometry: the WF&S's route into Wichita Falls (Southern Junction, MP 39.8, to the Wichita Falls station, MP 35.9) and its Wichita Falls, Breckenridge and Dublin station sites are not located; the Wichita Falls end is a 2.7 mi straight line from the city-centre geocode.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout; the only timings found are two 1920 Breckenridge departures (WFR&FW) and the 1942 Nos. 41/42 at Wichita Falls.
metadata.omitted: Block [2] Wichita Falls - Newcastle under the Katy of Texas, 1914-1920 (no confirmed passenger year); block [3] Wichita Falls - Newcastle under the WF&S Railway again, 1 Mar 1920 - 30 Jun 1921 (no confirmed passenger year); block [6]'s 1921-1927 era on Jimkurn - Breckenridge (operator of the passenger trains unresolved) - that 9 mi piece is drawn only within the 1929-1942 WF&S Wichita Falls - Breckenridge feature; block [9] WF&S trackage rights Wichita Falls - Waurika, OK, from 1927 (no WF&S passenger use found); the 1952-1954 freight-only final years and the Rock Island's Graham - south of Breckenridge freight operation 1954-1969 (Rule 1); Newcastle mine tracks and other industrial spurs (freight only); the Eastland, Wichita Falls & Gulf, the Wichita Falls & Oklahoma, the Wichita Falls Railway and the Wichita Falls & Northwestern (separate roads).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Written passenger-only from the start: no freight-only segments or features. Post-passenger freight (to the 1954 abandonment) and the Rock Island's 1954-69 Graham - Breckenridge freight line are not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable: steam from opening (Dublin Citizen); diesel from 1953.
metadata.line_label_audit: Written to Rule 6 from the start.

properties.line: Wichita Falls and Southern: Wichita Falls – Newcastle
properties.speed_source: Estimate (Rule 3): no 1909 running time was found. 35 km/h is a typical figure for a short Texas steam branch with one train a day each way.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, half-degree `way["railway"]` tiles because 1-degree tiles 504'd) plus OpenHistoricalMap, traced with opstrace.py. Only one OSM way carries a WF&S old_railway_operator (103488523, `old_railway_operator=WF&S`, south of Breckenridge). North of Breckenridge the grade survives as UNTAGGED OSM ways: 151833278 (railway=abandoned, 59.6 mi, Wichita Falls outskirts - Archer City - Olney - Newcastle - Graham) and 151833274 (railway=razed, 45.3 mi, Graham - Eliasville - south of Breckenridge, the stretch the Rock Island kept as a freight line 1954-69). At the Wichita Falls end the OSM grade stops short, and OHM way 202454953 ('Wichita Falls and Southern Railway', start_date 1908-09) carries it about 3 mi further toward town. OHM names were costed as successors (2x) so the denser OSM grade was preferred wherever both exist. Identified as the WF&S because the ways run Wichita Falls - Archer City - Olney - Newcastle - Graham - Breckenridge as one continuous grade that no other road built, and the traced length matches the ICC/Fowler mileage. Waypoints: Nominatim for Wichita Falls, Archer City, Olney, Newcastle, Graham, Breckenridge (all checked: town boundaries, not counties), Anarene, South Bend, Eliasville (hamlets), plus the OHM grade's north end (33.8834, -98.5333); Tobin (geocoded to Austin), Bullock (wrong county) and Lake Wichita (the reservoir) were rejected; Jimkurn did not geocode.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 54.5 mi against a documented 52.4 mi (ICC vol. 34 owned line, 52.426) / 55.1 mi (Fowler mileposts, Wichita Falls station 35.9 to Newcastle 91.0). About 48.8 mi on the untagged abandoned OSM grade 151833278 and 3.0 mi on OHM 202454953; one approximated leg: a 2.7 mi straight line from central Wichita Falls (city-centre geocode, 33.9005, -98.5021) south-west to the grade at 33.874, -98.536. It stands in for the WF&S's entry into Wichita Falls, which per Fowler's mileposts was 3.9 mi from the Wichita Falls station to Southern Junction (MP 35.9 -> 39.8), presumably over another road's track; neither that route nor the WF&S's Wichita Falls station (a separate depot by 1942) is located. Waypoint fit: Archer City 0.3, Anarene 0.0, Olney 0.6, Newcastle 0.6 km from the line. Draws the alignment as finally abandoned in 1954; no realignment is known.

segments.note: The Wichita Falls and Southern Railway (inc. 1 Jun 1907; Kemp, Kell, Kempner), Wichita Falls - Lake Wichita - Archer City - Olney - Orth - Newcastle, built to the Newcastle coal field. 1909 [ANCHOR]: the only year of this operator era confirmed for passengers. Fowler records three station names on this line as printed in the 1909 Official Guide ('South Junction 1909G', 'Lakeview 1909G', 'Wilson 1909G', i.e. Southern Junction, Lake Wichita, Luke Wilson), a public-timetable listing. Service certainly ran wider in both directions, but no other year of the WF&S Railway's own operation (1 Jan 1909 - 30 Apr 1914, ICC vol. 34) is confirmed, so do not widen this anchor. Opening conflict recorded, not resolved: TSHA says completed to New Castle by Sept 1908; ICC vol. 34 says 'completed and placed in operation on January 1, 1909' (the later date is drawn). The Katy's 1911 stock purchase did not change who ran the trains and is not a split. From 1 May 1914 to 29 Feb 1920 the Katy of Texas (USRA 1918-20) operated the line under lease, and the WF&S Railway ran it again 1 Mar 1920 - 30 Jun 1921; no passenger year is confirmed in either era, so neither is drawn. headway_min 1440 (one train a day) is an estimate - no 1909 timetable was found.
sources: Segment-level: 1909 rests on Fowler's '1909G' Official Guide station-name annotations for this line; the operator era and opening date are from ICC Valuation Reports vol. 34 and TSHA (opening-date conflict recorded). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Wichita Falls and Southern Railroad (inc. 1 Nov 1920), Wichita Falls - Archer City - Olney - Newcastle - Graham - Eliasville - Jimkurn - Breckenridge. The Railroad built Newcastle - Jimkurn (opened 1 Jul 1921, ICC vol. 44), leased the WF&S Railway's Wichita Falls - Newcastle line from 1 Jul 1921 (re-leased 1 Jul 1927) and ran the Wichita Falls, Ranger & Fort Worth's Jimkurn - Breckenridge piece from 1 Sep 1927; the three companies merged 31 Dec 1940. The 1921 lease of the Railway is the same Kell-Kemp company and is not a split. START 1929 [OPEN]: the first CONFIRMED passenger year, and it rests on system-level evidence only - TSHA gives the WF&S Railroad $81,082 passenger revenue and 5 passenger cars in 1929, for the Wichita Falls - Dublin road it then ran, without naming segments. Trains almost certainly ran from the July 1921 opening, but 1921-1928 is not confirmed and who ran passenger trains over Jimkurn - Breckenridge before Sep 1927 is unresolved, so it is not drawn. END 1942 [OPEN]: the Wichita Falls depot listing for 1942 (chicagorailfan, a secondary source that cites no timetable) shows WF&S mixed No. 41 leaving 10:00 am for Breckenridge and No. 42 arriving 9:30 pm, and says the WF&S had moved to a separate station. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source with a primary citation dates when passenger service stopped. Evidence after 1942: chicagorailfan says passenger service was discontinued in 1950 (no source); the Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints a 'Breckenridge to Wichita Falls' table under a WF&S heading dated April 1951, but its times did not survive OCR; TSHA gives 1952 revenue as freight and 'other' only. Do not extend without evidence. A stricter reading would draw only 1942 [ANCHOR], the one segment-specific year; 1929-1942 follows the research report's drawable span. The road was abandoned in 1954 (an abandonment year, not a passenger end); the Rock Island then ran Graham - south of Breckenridge as a freight line to 1969, which is not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 1440 (one mixed round trip a day, 1942) is an estimate: days of operation are not stated, and 1929 frequency is unknown.
sources: Segment-level: start year from TSHA's 1929 WF&S Railroad passenger revenue (system-level, not specific to this segment); end year from the 1942 Wichita Falls depot listing on chicagorailfan (secondary, no timetable cited). Operator dates from ICC Valuation Reports vol. 44. Headway not sourced beyond the 1942 listing.

Breckenridge - Dublin is OSM way 103488523 (railway=abandoned, `old_railway_operator=WF&S`, 58.2 mi from just south of Breckenridge to Dublin) plus the south end of the untagged razed way 151833274 (and its 0.5 mi stub 151830256) through Breckenridge. OHM ways 202454954/202454956/202454957 ('Wichita Falls, Ranger and Fort Worth Railroad') follow the same grade and agree. It stays on its own grade past Ranger; the Texas & Pacific and the Katy/Cisco lines were not used. Waypoints Breckenridge, Ranger, Dublin (towns), Frankell, Desdemona (hamlets) from Nominatim.

About 58.2 mi on OSM way 103488523 (old_railway_operator=WF&S) and 6.0 mi on the south end of untagged razed OSM way 151833274 through Breckenridge. No approximated (straight-line) legs. segments.note: Wichita Falls, Ranger & Fort Worth Railroad (inc. 26 Sep 1919; Jake L. Hamon chief promoter), Breckenridge - Breckwalker - Frankell - Ranger - Desdemona - Jakehamon - Neff - Dublin, built in the Ranger oil boom. START 1920: ICC vol. 44 has the first 30.60 mi placed in operation 7 Apr 1920 and the last section 1 Mar 1921; the Breckenridge Texan reports the first train into Breckenridge on 30 Jun 1920 with passenger coaches and through Breckenridge - Dublin service 'by June 27, 1920' (the article's own dates conflict by three days; both are 1920). The Dublin Citizen recalls 'the first passenger train that arrived in Dublin in 1920'; a typical train had three passenger cars and a baggage car. 1921: Fowler records 'Plateau 1921G', a station on this line in the 1921 Official Guide. 1926: TSHA gives WFR&FW passenger revenue $4,699 and three passenger cars, and the WFR&FW built a small Dublin passenger station that summer after the Frisco evicted it from its Dublin freight station. The receivership of 26 Dec 1921 - 31 Mar 1926 is not a split. END 1926 [OPEN]: the last CONFIRMED year of the WFR&FW's own operation, which ran to 31 Aug 1927 (ICC); Jan-Aug 1927 is unconfirmed, so this is not a known end. Do not extend without evidence. From 1 Sep 1927 the Wichita Falls & Southern Railroad ran the line (see the WF&S Breckenridge - Dublin feature). The WFR&FW also operated the Eastland, Wichita Falls & Gulf under lease 1 Jun 1921 - 19 Mar 1922; that is a separate road and is not drawn here. headway_min 720 is an estimate from two 1920 departures from Breckenridge (No. 4 6:10 am, No. 8 8:30 pm); frequency in 1921-26 is not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1920 from the Breckenridge Texan and Dublin Citizen opening accounts and ICC vol. 44; 1921 from Fowler's 'Plateau 1921G'; 1926 from TSHA's WFR&FW passenger revenue. Operator end (31 Aug 1927) from ICC vol. 44. Headway estimated from the two 1920 departure times.

segments.note: Wichita Falls & Southern Railroad operation of the WFR&FW's Breckenridge - Ranger - Dublin line (lease from 1 Jul 1927; ICC vol. 44: 'operations did not commence until September 1, 1927'; merged into the WF&S Railroad 31 Dec 1940). 1929 [ANCHOR]: the only proven year, and it rests on system-level evidence - TSHA gives the WF&S Railroad $81,082 passenger revenue and 5 passenger cars in 1929 for the whole Wichita Falls - Dublin road, without naming segments. Service certainly ran wider than 1929 both ways but no other year is confirmed: nothing segment-specific was found after the WFR&FW's 1926 figures. The 1942 mixed train listed at Wichita Falls ran only to Breckenridge. The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints a WF&S 'Dublin to Breckenridge' table headed 'Monday, Wednesday, Friday' (schedules dated April 1951), but no times survived OCR, so 1951 is neither confirmed nor denied. A diesel was put on Ranger - Dublin in Sep 1953 for what was by then a freight railroad; the line was abandoned in 1954. Neither is a passenger end. Do not widen this anchor without evidence. The Dublin end connected with the Santa Fe (GC&SF) and the Katy, and Ranger with the Texas & Pacific. headway_min 1440 is an estimate; 1929 frequency is not sourced.
